content:
#42962 made me discover a case where I believe a lemma is privately transitively imported, but not publically.
More specifically, this code works

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.GeomSum
import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic

#check Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div

but the equivalent module system version fails:

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.GeomSum
public import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic

/-- error: Unknown constant `Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div` -/
#guard_msgs in
#check Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div

If I suspect there's some non-public import somewhere in the transitive import closure of this test file, how would I investigate this best? (I don't remember the current incantation to generate the import graph from the module defining Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div to my module, for instance: presumably, that would already help.)

The incantation is

lake exe graph ./import-graph.pdf --from Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.GeomSum

though you could also load the full import graph into Python's networkx if it helps
cc: @Thomas Murrills who has been studying imports recently.

The chain here is

Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Finprod
Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.GroupWithZero.Action
Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Expect
Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic

and the 2nd module imports the 1st privately

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

cc: Thomas Murrills who has been studying imports recently.

Ah yeah, this is a pretty cool problem. I think I'll be able to handle this sort of thing through the infra I'm building out on top of shake :) (Though, fwiw, I'm working on using that infra in different tooling first! So maybe in a little while. Also deserves some thought as to whether the UX should answer questions like this directly, or through more general import-hierarchy inspection UX)

If your question is "how can I quickly locate the missing import", then this works:

import Mathlib

public abbrev test := @Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div

giving

Note: A public declaration Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div exists but is imported privately; consider adding public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset.
(You can also find the source file just by hovering over the declaration in the working non-module version :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:)
These seem different from finding the intermediate private import than Snir pointed out though, right? This is how I interpreted Michael's question.
I know how to find the import, if only by loogleing for the declaration. That was not the question :-)
Thanks everybody for the help and the answers!

here's a trick you can do:

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.GeomSum
import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic

/--
error: Declaration @Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div is not allowed to be imported by this file.
It is defined in Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset,
  which is imported by Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Finprod,
  which is imported by Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.GroupWithZero.Action,
  which is imported by Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Expect,
  which is imported by Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic,
  which is imported by this file.

These invariants are maintained by `assert_not_exists` statements, and exist in order to ensure that "complicated" parts of the library are not accidentally introduced as dependencies of "simple" parts of the library.
-/
#guard_msgs in
assert_not_exists Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div
